name: Defence

scores.why: Power side-channel anomaly detection as an independent check on what device software reports, with alerts sent over a separate authenticated LoRa path. Rare at a hackathon, though power-based intrusion detection exists in research.
Fits 'detect earlier' and keeps working when IP networks are compromised or down: the LoRa link is treated as hostile, every frame is signed and encrypted, and replays are rejected.
Systemd installers, node enrollment and an operations runbook, but each monitored device needs its own current sensor and USB oscilloscope, and the detector is a simple CUSUM on mean voltage.
Polished landing page with an isometric solar-field illustration, a 75-second captioned film and a hand-built command-console dashboard.
The whole chain is in code (ESP32 firmware, acquisition, CUSUM voting, crypto protocol, SQLite, Flask API, dashboard); no tests and duplicated node code.

projects.verdict: Strong, genuinely built defensive prototype that fits the brief; held back by a staged anomaly, simple detection and no tests.

name: Artificial Intelligence

scores.why: Per-phoneme GOP over a curated confusion set on an LM-free wav2vec2 phoneme CTC model (server/app/scoring/gop.py) so substitutions aren't auto-corrected, plus per-child threshold calibration from therapist overrides (calibration.py), phonemizer-validated LLM word suggestions (llm/validators.py) and self-QA of ElevenLabs audio with the own scorer. Speech-therapy apps exist, but explicit 'heard S instead of SZ' for Polish is a fresh angle.

Hits nearly every brief point: README 'Gdzie jest AI' table shows the AI's role and component fit, docs explain technical decisions and limits, and user control is concrete (niepewne verdict, confidence, per-attempt playback, therapist override in AttemptsTable.tsx) with one concrete use case (Zosia practising SZ).

Addresses a real gap (home practice between weekly therapy sessions, therapist-driven, local audio, no child name sent to the LLM), but only SZ and R are covered, eval/results.md is 1 adult imitating errors (no children), and it requires a local Python server with a 1.2 GB model.

Screenshots show a polished, consistent child app (custom animated lynx mascot, lesson path, mouth-position hint, no punishments) and a professional therapist dashboard with a sound × position heatmap and per-attempt table; mobile layouts too.

~9.4k real LOC across a React front end and a FastAPI server, 60 tests (server/tests), a reproducible eval harness and a live-session write-up; however the Claude path ran only from a hand-written cache, eval recordings are gitignored, and the live demo is down.

Each new target needs a new guest program and deployment; proving is slow and needs Linux/Docker; writing the bug rule is hard for maintainers.
A zero-knowledge proof-of-exploit bounty that also encrypts the finding to the maintainer inside the proved computation is rare and well thought out.

193 test functions over 4.2k lines, 326 passed in recorded evidence, 8 policy tests in real OPA, plus a 48-case EN/PL live evaluation reported honestly.
Drop-in OpenAI base URL plus MCP endpoint, make targets, Docker compose with Ollama and OPA. Single node, budgets count tokens not money, local feed file.
